thread:
alejandro: paging: p99 spike on streaming tail in us-west-2 starting ~2026-03-15T12:03Z. alerts show streaming p95->1200ms, p99->4.2s. dashboards point to control-plane RPCs (config-fetch + featureflag) spiking concurrently. not sure yet if auth ratelimit or db contention.
maria: seeing same. trace IDs: trace-9f3a, trace-9f3b. most affected route /v1/streaming/generate. traffic volume normal.
incident-bot: INCIDENT(Severity=high) created by monitoring@redwood — streaming-p99-spike-us-west-2. Pager sent to oncall.
oncall: I'm on it. sharing initial runbook steps.
sam: quick checks — redis cache hit rate for prefix-KV dropped from 98% -> 45% at 12:02. configstore latency (90th) jumped to 600ms, 99th to 2.3s. auth token fetch p99 also 1.1s.
jamie: logs show many configstore requests returning 503 and retries piling up. stack shows blocking call in inference-gateway waiting on configstore before allowed to stream.
lia: can we switch to cached config fallback? i.e., skip fresh config fetch for streaming requests for 30s and serve last-known config — low risk but avoids blocking.
maria: +1. adding command we can run to flip gate:
```
# enable degraded config fallback on gateway
curl -X POST "https://ops-api.internal/v1/featureflip" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPSTOKEN" -d '{"feature":"streaming_degraded_config_fallback","value":true}'
```
alejandro: run it now. also bump configstore client retry backoff to avoid thundering retries.
sam: applied fallback on prod-gateway-usw2. metrics: streaming tail p99 dropped from 4.2s -> 1.3s in ~45s.
jamie: opened ticket with infra-db: control-plane nginx pool is saturated; they saw a burst of traffic from canary tests at 12:00 that saturated the backend. ticket #INC-3421.
oncall: notify support & docs for customer impact? need customer-facing line.
lia: draft: "At 12:03 UTC we observed elevated streaming latency for a subset of requests in US-West due to backend configuration service overload. We activated a fallback to last-known configuration and rate-limited retries which mitigated the issue. Impact: brief elevated latency and streaming stalls for ~6k requests; no long-term data loss. We're continuing investigation and will post updates"
maria: send now.
deploy-bot: deploy 2136.1 to gateway-usw2 rolled back (reason: rollback requested by oncall).
alejandro: follow-ups: 1) add circuit-breaker in gateway for configstore calls (fail-fast after 100ms + fallback), 2) increase configstore pool, 3) limit internal canary burst to avoid saturation, 4) surface per-route fallback metrics.
sam: temporary mitigation applied: reduced client retries and enabled exponential backoff. also increased KV cache TTL from 5s -> 60s for streaming routes.
jamie: DB/infra confirmed they applied additional worker nodes and cleared backlog; configstore 99th latency now 220ms.
oncall: handing off to night oncall @lia. summary in incident doc: https://internal.redwood/incidents/2136789012. please monitor p99 and support queue.
lia: ack — will monitor and escalate if symptoms return. plan to validate no regressions on canary tomorrow.
incident-bot: INCIDENT updates: severity downgraded to medium. mitigation in place.
maria: action items captured: alex/circuit-breaker PR, infra/scale configstore, devex/rate-limit canary. assigning owners in docs.
alejandro: one customer impact follow-up: run eval on affected tenants to ensure no degraded model outputs due to config fallback. reach out if any anomalies.
lia: leaving handoff note for next oncall: if p99>1.5s alert, revert fallback off and throttle canaries.
sam: logs / grep snippet showing 503 spike:
```
2026-03-15T12:01:58Z gateway-usw2 inference-gateway [warn] configstore call failed status=503 retry=1 id=trace-9f3a
2026-03-15T12:02:02Z gateway-usw2 inference-gateway [warn] configstore call failed status=503 retry=2 id=trace-9f3b
```
maria: closing notes: mitigation reduced customer-visible tails. will follow with RCA draft focused on (1) canary isolation, (2) fail-fast + fallback, (3) telemetry gaps on per-route config latency.
alejandro: thanks all. moving to post-incident review tomorrow. :party_parrot:
